claim: AAV-shPtbp1 and AAV-shscramble were designed under the full-length (2.2 kb) GFAP promoter.
source: To effectively repress astroglial PTBP1 in vivo, we designed and synthesized AAV (serotype 2/5) expressing EGFP, followed by shRNA targeting mouse Ptbp1 as previously reported (Qian et al., 2020), under the full-length (2.2 kb) GFAP promoter (AAV-shPtbp1). The corresponding virus expressing scramble shRNA (AAV-shscramble) was used as a control (Figure 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in the text describing the AAV vector design.

claim: Both AAV-shPtbp1 and AAV-shscramble predominantly infected astrocytes 7 days post-infection.
source: Our results showed that both AAVs mostly infected astrocytes (AldoC+), but not neurons (neuronal nuclei, NeuN+), NG2-glia (NG2+), or microglia (Iba-1+) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data and cell counting shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: AAV-shPtbp1 downregulated PTBP1 expression to undetectable levels in GFP+ cells from 1 to 3 months.
source: PTBP1 expression was not affected by AAV-shscramble, but was downregulated to undetectable levels by AAV-shPtbp1 in GFP+ cells from 1 to 3 months (Figure 1B, C), indicating astroglial PTBP1 was consistently repressed.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining and quantification in Figure 1B, C showing PTBP1 levels over time.

claim: GFP+NeuN+ cells were detected at 12.65 ± 1.56%, 41.10 ± 1.98%, and 46.09 ± 12.9% at 1, 2, and 3 months after AAV-shPtbp1 injection in the substantia nigra.
source: The results showed that very few GFP+NeuN+ cells (approximately 2.39%) were detected even at 3 months after AAV-shscramble injection, while remarkable GFP+NeuN+ cells were detected, with 12.65 ± 1.56%, 41.10 ± 1.98%, and 46.09 ± 12.9% GFP+ cells expressing NeuN, and with 8.99 ± 1.99%, 30.40 ± 3.03%, and 37.93 ± 9.92% expressed TH, at 1, 2, and 3 months after AAV-shPtbp1 injection in the substantial nigra (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: GFP+TH+ cells were detected at 8.99 ± 1.99%, 30.40 ± 3.03%, and 37.93 ± 9.92% at 1, 2, and 3 months after AAV-shPtbp1 injection in the substantia nigra.
source: The results showed that very few GFP+NeuN+ cells (approximately 2.39%) were detected even at 3 months after AAV-shscramble injection, while remarkable GFP+NeuN+ cells were detected, with 12.65 ± 1.56%, 41.10 ± 1.98%, and 46.09 ± 12.9% GFP+ cells expressing NeuN, and with 8.99 ± 1.99%, 30.40 ± 3.03%, and 37.93 ± 9.92% expressed TH, at 1, 2, and 3 months after AAV-shPtbp1 injection in the substantial nigra (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Only GFP+NeuN+ cells, but not GFP+TH+ cells, were detected in the striatum after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery.
source: In the striatum, only GFP+NeuN+ cells, but not GFP+TH+ cells, were detected after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: Immunostaining results shown in Figure 1E, F.

claim: The results of this study highly resemble results of Qian's study but are against that of Zhou's study.
source: These results highly resemble results of Qian's study (Qian et al., 2020) but against that of Zhou's study (Zhou et al., 2020).
evidence: Comparison with previous published studies.

claim: AAV-mediated gene expression could be 'leaked' into neurons.
source: However, these results are not sufficient to prove that astrocytes were truly converted to neurons including DAn, as AAV-mediated gene expression could be 'leaked' into neurons as indicated by a recent study (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: Referenced from a recent study by Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 mice have the highest specificity to target astrocytes.
source: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 mice with the highest specificity to target astrocytes (Srinivasan et al., 2016) were chosen to cross-breed with a reporter mouse Rpl22lsl-HA (Ribotag) (Sanz et al., 2009), in which the endogenous ribosomal protein Rpl22 was tagged with three copies of the hemagglutinin (HA) epitope after Cre-mediated recombination (Figure 2A).
evidence: Cited from Srinivasan et al., 2016.

claim: Almost all AldoC-positive astrocytes were specifically labeled with the HA epitope after Tamoxifen-mediated induction of CreERT2 activity.
source: After Tamoxifen (TAM)-mediated induction of CreERT2 activity, almost all of the AldoC-positive astrocytes were specifically labeled with the HA epitope (Figure 2B) and barely no HA leaky expression was observed in the neurons of the substantia nigra and striatum of Aldh1l1-CreERT2;Rpl22lsl-HA mice.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining in Figure 2B.

claim: Barely no HA leaky expression was observed in the neurons of the substantia nigra and striatum of Aldh1l1-CreERT2;Rpl22lsl-HA mice.
source: After Tamoxifen (TAM)-mediated induction of CreERT2 activity, almost all of the AldoC-positive astrocytes were specifically labeled with the HA epitope (Figure 2B) and barely no HA leaky expression was observed in the neurons of the substantia nigra and striatum of Aldh1l1-CreERT2;Rpl22lsl-HA mice.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining in Figure 2B.

claim: No GFP+TH+ or GFP+NeuN+ cells that were simultaneously HA-positive could be detected in AAV-shPtbp1 treated mice.
source: Through exhaustive examination of the whole midbrain and striatum, no GFP+TH+ or GFP+NeuN+ cells that were simultaneously HA-positive could be detected in either AAV-shPtbp1 (Figure 2D, E) or AAV-shscramble (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B) treated mice.
evidence: Exhaustive examination of immunostaining shown in Figure 2D, E.

claim: PTBP1 repression fails to convert quiescent astrocytes to neurons including dopaminergic neurons.
source: Therefore, the lineage-tracing results clearly illustrat that PTBP1 repression fails to convert quiescent astrocytes to neurons including DAns, which is consistent with recent studies (Wang et al., 2021; Blackshaw et al., 2021).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from lineage-tracing experiments and consistent with cited studies.

claim: Reactive astrocytes may acquire certain characteristics of neural stem cells upon brain injury.
source: During brain injury or neurodegeneration, astrocytes become activated and acquire certain characteristics of neural stem cells (NSCs) such as proliferation, Nestin- or Vimentin-immunoreactivity, and multipotency (Buffo et al., 2008; Shimada et al., 2012; Robel et al., 2011; Sirko et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Buffo et al., 2008; Shimada et al., 2012; Robel et al., 2011; Sirko et al., 2013).

claim: Reactive astrocytes with stem cell hallmarks can be reprogrammed to neurons more easily and efficiently than quiescent astrocytes.
source: Some researchers have claimed that reactive astrocytes with stem cell hallmarks can be reprogrammed to neurons more easily and efficiently than quiescent astrocytes (Grande et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2014; Brulet et al., 2017; Wan et al., 2014; Mattugini et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from multiple studies (Grande et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2014; Brulet et al., 2017; Wan et al., 2014; Mattugini et al., 2019).

claim: 6-OHDA induced severe lesions in the nigrostriatal pathway, characterized by significantly reduced numbers of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and remarkably decreased densities of TH+ fibers in the striatum.
source: Our results showed that 6-OHDA induced severe lesions in the nigrostriatal pathway, characterized by significantly reduced numbers of DAns in the substantia nigra and remarkably decreased densities of TH+ fibers in the striatum (Figure 3B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining in Figure 3B.

claim: Astrocytes became remarkably activated after 6-OHDA lesion, as indicated by hypertrophy of the main processes and cell bodies and upregulation of intermediate filament protein GFAP.
source: Meanwhile, astrocytes became remarkably activated, as indicated by classic cytoskeletal and morphological changes, including hypertrophy of the main processes and cell bodies and upregulation of intermediate filament protein GFAP (Figure 3B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining in Figure 3B.

claim: No NeuN+ neurons including TH+ dopaminergic neurons positive for HA could be detected after PTBP1 repression in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.
source: However, under such circumstance, no NeuN+ neurons including TH+ DAns positive for HA, could be detected, and no obvious morphological changes of astrocytes (indicated by HA staining) were observed after PTBP1 repression (Figure 3C), suggesting that neither AtoN nor astrocyte-to-DAn (AtoDAn) conversion occurred.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining in Figure 3C.

claim: The number of NeuN+ neurons did not increase after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery into the substantia nigra compared with AAV-shscramble delivery in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.
source: Moreover, the number of NeuN+ neurons (Figure 3D) and TH+ DAns (Figure 3E) did not increase after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery into the substantia nigra compared with AAV-shscramble delivery.
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The number of TH+ dopaminergic neurons did not increase after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery into the substantia nigra compared with AAV-shscramble delivery in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.
source: Moreover, the number of NeuN+ neurons (Figure 3D) and TH+ DAns (Figure 3E) did not increase after AAV-shPtbp1 delivery into the substantia nigra compared with AAV-shscramble delivery.
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The motor deficits induced by 6-OHDA lesion were not improved by AAV-shPtbp1 injection.
source: The motor deficits induced by 6-OHDA lesion (reflected by apomorphine-induced rotation) were not improved by AAV-shPtbp1 injection, either (Figure 3F).
evidence: Behavioral test data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Repressing PTBP1 fails to generate dopaminergic neurons from reactive astrocytes in a mouse 6-OHDA model of Parkinson's disease.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that repressing PTBP1 also fails to generate DAns from reactive astrocytes in a mouse 6-OHDA model of PD.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental data in the 6-OHDA model.

claim: ASO-Ptbp1 significantly downregulated astroglial PTBP1 for 2 months after delivery compared to ASO-Ctrl delivery.
source: Immunofluorescence results showed that ASO was distributed broadly in the midbrain, as indicated by ASO-attached Cy3, and astroglial PTBP1 was significantly downregulated for 2 months after ASO-Ptbp1 delivery compared to ASO-Ctrl delivery (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Western blot analysis confirmed the knockdown efficiency of ASO-Ptbp1 in the midbrain.
source: Western blot analysis of the midbrain further confirmed the knockdown efficiency of ASO-Ptbp1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, D).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, D.

claim: No astrocyte-originated neurons or dopaminergic neurons were found after ASO-Ptbp1 delivery in quiescent astrocytes.
source: Using brain slices from the same mice, we did not find any astrocyte-originated neurons (YFP+NeuN+) or DAns (YFP+TH+) (Figure 4B), suggesting that no neurons, including DAns, were converted from quiescent astrocytes after ASO-Ptbp1 delivery.
evidence: Immunostaining results shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No neurons including dopaminergic neurons positive for HA were generated from reactive astrocytes after ASO-Ptbp1 delivery in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.
source: Two months after ASO delivery, we still could not find any neurons including DAns positive for HA (Figure 4D), indicating that no neurons, including DAn, were generated from reactive astrocytes.
evidence: Immunostaining results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The motor deficits of the 6-OHDA lesioned mice were not alleviated by 2 months of ASO-Ptbp1 treatment.
source: Furthermore, the motor deficits of the 6-OHDA lesioned mice were not alleviated by 2 months of ASO-Ptbp1 treatment (Figure 4E), similar to those of ASO-Ctrl (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Behavioral test data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Repressing astroglial PTBP1 via ASO fails to generate dopaminergic neurons from either quiescent or reactive astrocytes in a 6-OHDA mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
source: These data demonstrate that repressing astroglial PTBP1 via ASO also fails to generate DAns from either quiescent or reactive astrocytes in a 6-OHDA mouse model of PD.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from ASO experiments.

claim: Neither AAV-shRNA- nor ASO-mediated astroglial PTBP1 repression could achieve astrocyte-to-neuron or astrocyte-to-dopaminergic neuron conversion in the substantia nigra or striatum of a 6-OHDA mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
source: In this study, through stringent and convincing lineage-tracing technology, we substantiated that neither AAV-shRNA- nor ASO-mediated astroglial PTBP1 repression could achieve AtoN or AtoDAn conversion either in the substantia nigra or in the striatum of a 6-OHDA mouse model of PD.
evidence: Summary conclusion of the study based on lineage-tracing experiments.

claim: AAV-shPtbp1 allowed for low levels of reporter protein (GFP) expression in neurons after 1–3 months of infection, whereas AAV-shscramble-mediated GFP expression was still restricted to astrocytes.
source: After 1–3 months of infection, AAV-shPtbp1 allowed for low levels of reporter protein (GFP) expression in neurons, whereas AAV-shscramble-mediated GFP expression was still restricted to astrocytes.
evidence: Observation from immunostaining experiments over time.

claim: The shPtbp1 sequence might function similarly to Neurod1, activating GFAP promoter and driving GFP expression in neurons at a relatively low level.
source: According to a recent study, coding sequences of some proneural genes, such as Neurod1, could activate GFAP promoter elements in cis and drive the expression of the viral reporter gene in neurons (Wang et al., 2021). We presume that the shPtbp1 sequence might function similarly to Neurod1, activating GFAP promoter and driving GFP expression in neurons at a relatively low level.
evidence: Speculation based on cited study (Wang et al., 2021).

claim: AAV can exert toxic effects on doublecortin (DCX)+ neuroblasts or neural progenitor cells.
source: It has been reported that AAV can exert toxic effects on doublecortin (DCX)+ neuroblasts or neural progenitor cells (Johnston et al., 2021), which might render the virus-infected astrocytes unable to convert into neurons.
evidence: Cited from Johnston et al., 2021.

claim: DCX+ intermediate cells could hardly be detected using AAV for gene manipulation in in vivo glia-to-neuron conversion studies.
source: After reviewing previous studies of in vivo glia-to-neuron conversion, we found that DCX+ intermediate cells could hardly be detected using AAV for gene manipulation (Liu et al., 2015; Guo et al., 2014; Brulet et al., 2017; Mattugini et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; Lai et al., 2020; Leib et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2020; Xiang et al., 2021; Zheng et al., 2022; Torper et al., 2015; Pereira et al., 2017).
evidence: Observation from reviewing multiple cited studies.

claim: DCX+ intermediate cells can usually be seen in most lentivirus/retrovirus-mediated glia-to-neuron conversion studies in vivo.
source: In contrast, DCX+ intermediate cells can usually be seen in most lentivirus (LV)/retrovirus (RV)-mediated glia-to-neuron conversion studies in vivo (Grande et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2014; Niu et al., 2013; Buffo et al., 2005; Gascón et al., 2016; Torper et al., 2013; Rivetti di Val Cervo et al., 2017; Magnusson et al., 2014; Niu et al., 2015; Su et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2022; Heinrich et al., 2014).
evidence: Observation from reviewing multiple cited studies.

claim: Either AAV toxicity restrains the astrocyte-to-neuron conversion process, or lentivirus/retrovirus boosts the astrocyte-to-neuron conversion process in an unknown manner.
source: This observation suggests that either AAV toxicity restrains the AtoN conversion process, or LV/RV boosts the AtoN conversion process in an unknown manner.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation about DCX+ cells in different viral systems.

claim: The result of Qian et al., 2020 is not convincing since the reporter mice Rosa-Tdtomato (Ai14) used for lineage-tracing has been questioned for occasional leakage to neurons.
source: This result is inconsistent with that of a previous study claiming that AtoN conversion occurred after ASO-Ptbp1 delivery (Qian et al., 2020). However, we believe that their result is not convincing since the reporter mice-Rosa-Tdtomato (Ai14) used for lineage-tracing by Qian et al., 2020 has been questioned for occasional leakage to neurons (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: Critique based on cited study (Wang et al., 2021) questioning the reporter mouse used by Qian et al., 2020.

claim: Acute lesions induced by neurotoxins, such as 6-OHDA, usually result in substantial neuron loss, creating an inflammatory microenvironment characterized by the presence of both A1 (pro-inflammatory) and A2 (anti-inflammatory) astrocyte subtypes.
source: Acute lesions induced by neurotoxins, such as 6-OHDA, usually results in substantial neuron loss, creating an inflammatory microenvironment characterized by the presence of both A1 (pro-inflammatory) and A2 (anti-inflammatory) astrocyte subtypes (Ryu et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Ryu et al., 2020.

claim: Normal aging induces pro-inflammatory A1 like astrocyte reactivity.
source: In contrast, as one of the most important risk factors for PD, normal aging induces pro-inflammatory A1 like astrocyte reactivity (Clarke et al., 2018), which may accurately reflect the real state of PD patients.
evidence: Cited from Clarke et al., 2018.

claim: During ischemia stroke, astrocytes spontaneously become neurogenic and the Notch pathway is repressed.
source: In particular, during ischemia stroke, a classic model characterized by the presence of A2 astrocytes, astrocytes spontaneously become neurogenic and the Notch pathway is repressed (Magnusson et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from Magnusson et al., 2014.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), could be detrimental to the astrocyte-to-neuron conversion process and the survival, maturation, and subsequent neurite outgrowth of the newborn neurons.
source: We therefore assume that pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), could be detrimental to the AtoN conversion process and the survival, maturation, and subsequent neurite outgrowth of the newborn neurons (Karimi-Abdolrezaee and Billakanti, 2012; Belenguer et al., 2021; Park and Bowers, 2010), whereas the anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors, such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor might be beneficial and even critical (Niu et al., 2013).
evidence: Speculation based on cited studies (Karimi-Abdolrezaee and Billakanti, 2012; Belenguer et al., 2021; Park and Bowers, 2010).

claim: Anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors, such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor might be beneficial and even critical for astrocyte-to-neuron conversion.
source: We therefore assume that pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), could be detrimental to the AtoN conversion process and the survival, maturation, and subsequent neurite outgrowth of the newborn neurons (Karimi-Abdolrezaee and Billakanti, 2012; Belenguer et al., 2021; Park and Bowers, 2010), whereas the anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors, such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor might be beneficial and even critical (Niu et al., 2013).
evidence: Speculation based on cited study (Niu et al., 2013).

claim: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 transgenic mice were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Stock number #029655).
source: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 transgenic mice (Stock number #029655), Rpl22 lsl-HA (Ribotag) mice (Stock number #011029), and Rosa26lsl-YFP mice (Stock number #006148) were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Rpl22 lsl-HA (Ribotag) mice were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Stock number #011029).
source: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 transgenic mice (Stock number #029655), Rpl22 lsl-HA (Ribotag) mice (Stock number #011029), and Rosa26lsl-YFP mice (Stock number #006148) were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Rosa26lsl-YFP mice were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Stock number #006148).
source: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 transgenic mice (Stock number #029655), Rpl22 lsl-HA (Ribotag) mice (Stock number #011029), and Rosa26lsl-YFP mice (Stock number #006148) were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Tamoxifen was orally administered at a daily dose of 100 mg/kg body weight for 5 consecutive days.
source: TAM was orally administered at a daily dose of 100 mg/kg body weight for 5 consecutive days.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: 6-OHDA was dissolved in ice-cold saline solution (0.9% NaCl) containing 0.2 mg/mL L-Ascorbic acid at a concentration of 3 mg/mL.
source: In brief, 6-OHDA (Sigma, Shanghai, China) was dissolved in ice-cold saline solution (0.9% NaCl) containing 0.2 mg/mL L-Ascorbic acid (BBI Life Sciences, Shanghai, China) at a concentration of 3 mg/mL.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: 1 μL of 6-OHDA solution (3 μg) was delivered into the right medial forebrain bundle at a speed of 100 nL/min.
source: After anesthetized with 3% isoflurane, mice were then placed in a stereotaxic instrument (Model 940, Kopf Instruments, Tujunga, CA, USA) and delivered with 1 μL of 6-OHDA solution (3 μg) into the right medial forebrain bundle (mFB) at a speed of 100 nL/min according to the following coordinates: anteroposterior (A/P) = –1.20 mm, mediolateral (M/L) = 1.30 mm, dorsoventral (D/V) = –4.75 mm.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The coordinates for 6-OHDA injection into the medial forebrain bundle were anteroposterior (A/P) = –1.20 mm, mediolateral (M/L) = 1.30 mm, dorsoventral (D/V) = –4.75 mm.
source: After anesthetized with 3% isoflurane, mice were then placed in a stereotaxic instrument (Model 940, Kopf Instruments, Tujunga, CA, USA) and delivered with 1 μL of 6-OHDA solution (3 μg) into the right medial forebrain bundle (mFB) at a speed of 100 nL/min according to the following coordinates: anteroposterior (A/P) = –1.20 mm, mediolateral (M/L) = 1.30 mm, dorsoventral (D/V) = –4.75 mm.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: AAV-shPtbp1 has a titer of 3.41E+12 vg/mL.
source: To effectively repress astroglial PTBP1 in vivo, we designed and synthesized AAV (serotype 2/5) expressing EGFP, followed by shRNA targeting mouse Ptbp1 (5ʹ-GGGTGAAGATCCTGTTCAATA-3ʹ) as previously reported (Qian et al., 2020), under the full-length (2.2 kb) GFAP (human glial fibrillary acidic protein) promoter (AAV2/5-GFAP-EGFP-5'miR-30a-shRNA(Ptbp1)–3'miR-30a-WPREs, AAV-shPtbp1 for short, titer: 3.41E+12 vg/mL).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: AAV-shscramble has a titer of 2.57E+12 vg/mL.
source: The corresponding virus expressing scramble shRNA (same nucleotide composition but in a different sequence order) was used as a control (AAV2/5-GFAP-EGFP-5'miR-30a-shRNA(scramble)–3'miR-30a-WPREs, AAV-shscramble for short, titer: 2.57E+12 vg/mL) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Both AAVs were packaged by BrainVTA Co., Ltd (Wuhan, China).
source: Both AAVs were synthesized based on the pAAV-GFAP-EGFP-WPRE-hGH plasmid (Addgene #105549) and packaged by BrainVTA Co., Ltd (Wuhan, China).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The coordinates for AAV injection into the substantia nigra were A/P = –2.90 mm, M/L = 1.30 mm, and D/V = –4.35 mm.
source: The coordinates indicating distance from bregma were A/P = –2.90 mm, M/L = 1.30 mm, and D/V = –4.35 mm for the substantia nigra, and A/P = 0.80 mm, M/L = 1.60 mm, and D/V = –2.80 mm for the striatum.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The coordinates for AAV injection into the striatum were A/P = 0.80 mm, M/L = 1.60 mm, and D/V = –2.80 mm.
source: The coordinates indicating distance from bregma were A/P = –2.90 mm, M/L = 1.30 mm, and D/V = –4.35 mm for the substantia nigra, and A/P = 0.80 mm, M/L = 1.60 mm, and D/V = –2.80 mm for the striatum.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: ASO-Ptbp1 sequence is 5ʹ-GTGGAAATATTGCTAGGCAC-3ʹ.
source: ASOs were synthesized by Synbio Technology (Suzhou, China), the sequence and modification for ASO-Ptbp1 (5ʹ-GTGGAAATATTGCTAGGCAC-3ʹ) and control ASO (5ʹ-CCTATAGGACTATCCAGGAA-3ʹ) were performed as reported (Maimon et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Control ASO sequence is 5ʹ-CCTATAGGACTATCCAGGAA-3ʹ.
source: ASOs were synthesized by Synbio Technology (Suzhou, China), the sequence and modification for ASO-Ptbp1 (5ʹ-GTGGAAATATTGCTAGGCAC-3ʹ) and control ASO (5ʹ-CCTATAGGACTATCCAGGAA-3ʹ) were performed as reported (Maimon et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: 10 core 2ʹ-deoxyribonucleotides in the central of ASOs were flanked on both 5ʹ and 3ʹ sides by 5 2ʹ-methoxyethyl (MOE)-modified nucleotides.
source: Briefly, 10 core 2ʹ-deoxyribonucleotides in the central were flanked on both 5ʹ and 3ʹ sides by 5 2ʹ-methoxyethyl (MOE)-modified nucleotides.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The backbones of all ASOs contain phosphorothioate modifications and all cytosine residues were modified as 5ʹ-methylcytosines.
source: The backbones of all ASOs contain phosphorothioate modifications and all cytosine residues were modified as 5ʹ-methylcytosines.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Cyanine dye Cy3 was attached to the 3ʹ end of ASOs for fluorescence detection.
source: Cyanine dye Cy3 was attached to the 3ʹ end of those ASOs for fluorescence detection.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A 2 μL of ASO was injected into the substantia nigra at coordinates A/P = –2.90 mm, M/L = 1.30 mm, and D/V = –4.35 mm.
source: A 2 μL of ASO was injected into the substantia nigra (A/P = –2.90 mm, M/L = 1.30 mm, and D/V = –4.35 mm) of astrocyte-specific lineage-tracing mice with or without 6-OHDA lesion.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Mice were perfused intracardially with ice-cold phosphate buffered saline, followed by 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS at a flow rate of 10 mL/min.
source: For immunofluorescent analysis, mice were anesthetized with 1.25% Avertin and were perfused intracardially with ice-cold phosphate buffered saline (PBS), followed by 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA, Sigma, China) in PBS at a flow rate of 10 mL/min.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The brains were post-fixed in 4% PFA at 4°C overnight (8–12 hrs), followed by immersion in 20 and 30% sucrose for 24 hrs respectively.
source: The brains were then removed and post-fixed in 4% PFA at 4°C overnight (8–12 hrs), followed by immersion in 20 and 30% sucrose for 24 hrs respectively.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Cryostat-coronal sections encompassing the entire midbrain (20 μm) and striatum (30 μm) were serially collected.
source: In brief, cryostat-coronal sections encompassing the entire midbrain (20 μm) and striatum (30 μm) were serially collected.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Free-floating sections were pre-incubated in blocking solution containing 5% normal donkey serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 in 50 mM Tris-buffered saline (pH = 7.4) at room temperature for 1 hr.
source: Free-floating sections were pre-incubated in blocking solution containing 5% normal donkey serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 in 50 mM Tris-buffered saline (pH = 7.4) at room temperature for 1 hr.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Primary antibodies were incubated with sections overnight at 4°C.
source: Primary antibodies against HA tag (Rabbit, Abcam, ab9110, 1:1000), GFP (Rabbit, Abcam, ab290, 1:1000), GFP (Chicken, Abcam, ab13970, 1:1000), TH (Chicken, Millipore, AB9702, 1:1000), NeuN (Mouse IgG1, Millipore, MAB377, 1:1000), and PTBP1 (Rabbit, Invitrogen, PA5-81297, 1:1000) were dissolved in diluent and incubated with sections overnight at 4°C.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Secondary antibodies conjugated with Alexa 488, Alexa 555, or Alexa 647 were incubated at room temperature for 1 hr.
source: After washing three times, sections were incubated with the secondary antibodies (Thermo Fisher or Jackson ImmunoResearch), which were conjugated with Alexa 488, Alexa 555, or Alexa 647 at room temperature for 1 hr.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A 12 μm thick confocal Z-stack was acquired using ×63 objective.
source: A 12 μm thick confocal Z-stack was acquired using ×63 objective.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Three-dimensional reconstruction of z-stack images was generated using the Zeiss Zen software (blue edition).
source: Three-dimensional reconstruction of z-stack images was generated using the Zeiss Zen software (blue edition).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Statistical significance was considered when probability value of p<0.05.
source: For all analyses, statistical significance was considered when probability value of p<0.05.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods section.
